claim: ShortStack is a no-code platform for contests, sweepstakes, instant-win games, quizzes, landing pages and lead forms; claims 50,000+ businesses served over 15 years, with logos including Netflix, UFC, PetSmart, and Live Nation; embed-anywhere plus hosted landing pages.
page_title: Landing Pages & Contests Made Easy | ShortStack
notes: Homepage. Logos are marketing claims; Live Nation independently corroborated by case study (SHORTSTACK-014).

claim: Fraud/entry-integrity features: 'Fraud Filter' that 'identifies suspicious patterns, labels flagged entries, and silently rejects cheaters'; Google reCAPTCHA behavior analysis; Cloudflare Turnstile as CAPTCHA alternative.
notes: Marketing framing; mechanics confirmed in help doc (SHORTSTACK-012). No ML fraud scoring of its own — third-party CAPTCHA plus admin-authored patterns.

claim: Free standalone Rules Generator (no signup) produces full official rules + short-form social rules from a questionnaire: promotion type (sweepstakes vs contest), entry method, sponsor legal name/address, timeline with timezone, eligibility (age, US states/DC, Canada with mandatory skill-testing question, Quebec excluded), prizes/ARV, winner selection. Includes state registration-threshold warnings (New York, Florida referenced). Disclaimers: 'ShortStack is not a law firm and does not provide legal advice'; output is a 'starting-point template only, provided AS IS'; 'strongly recommends having a licensed attorney review your final rules'.
page_title: Free Contest & Sweepstakes Rules Generator | ShortStack
notes: Functional tool page, not just marketing. Standalone — not wired into campaign configuration or runtime enforcement.

claim: Compliance page covers data-privacy regimes only: GDPR, CCPA, PIPEDA, Australian Privacy Act, Nevada Privacy Law, UK/Swiss DPA; EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework certification; DPA, subprocessors list, UK SCCs, cookie policy. No promotion-law compliance features, no SOC 2 of its own, no age-gate/geo-restriction claims on this page.
notes: 'Compliance' at ShortStack means data privacy, not promotion/sweepstakes regulatory compliance.

claim: Security FAQs: AWS US hosting; SOC 2 Type II / ISO 27001 / PCI DSS attributed to the infrastructure provider (not ShortStack itself); TLS 1.2+, AES-256 at rest; annual third-party pen tests; quarterly internal reviews; access logged and reviewed every 6 months; critical patches in 24h; daily encrypted backups; deletion within 90 days of account closure; 48h breach notification; customer audit rights via DPA.
notes: Key nuance: certifications are the infrastructure provider's, indicating ShortStack has not obtained its own SOC 2 — a gap for enterprise procurement.

claim: Enterprise & Agencies offering: white label on own/client domains (custom emails, templates, favicon), multi-user roles/permissions, multi-team access, client folder management with unlimited campaigns and no per-client fees, dedicated Account Manager onboarding, custom campaign builds 'from concept to launch', claims handling 'millions of entries and traffic spikes'. No SSO, SLA, or named customers on the page.
notes: Professional services are campaign design/build services, not legal administration or winner/prize services.

claim: Public pricing: Free $0; Launch $24/mo annual; Build $49/mo (adds custom JavaScript, refer-a-friend, uploads); Scale $99/mo (adds multi-prize instant win, code redemption, 'Anti-fraud suite' = fraud filter + reCAPTCHA + country limits, 1 team seat); Max $166/mo (full white label, 'Entry API + advanced entry filtering', 3 team seats); overage rates per 10K views published; Enterprise = custom volume, custom agreements, dedicated AM; 50% non-profit discount.
notes: Feature gating evidence: API only at top self-serve tier; anti-fraud and geo 'country limits' are mid-tier marketing features, not a compliance module.

claim: Entries API is a read-only data-retrieval REST API: base https://entries.shortstack.com/entries; header auth 'Authorization: Token token=YOUR_API_KEY' (key created in API Explorer); filters for date ranges (received=), numeric ranges (age=18,), text search, export-profile field mapping; per_page default 100/max 5000; Link-header pagination; JSON {data:[...]} responses; plain-text errors with 401/404. Docs describe retrieval of collected entry data only — no campaign-management, decisioning, or entry-creation endpoints documented; no SDKs, versioning, idempotency, or rate limits documented.
notes: Help center behind Cloudflare challenge; direct fetch blocked (403). Details corroborated across multiple independent search snippets of the article. Confidence reduced accordingly.

claim: Outbound webhooks: HTTP POST of form data to a customer URL on each new entry; content types application/x-www-form-urlencoded or application/json; optional secret key produces HMAC-style signature in X-Ss-Signature header (request body + secret); Zapier/Make patterns documented for reaching other systems.
page_title: Securing Webhook Form Integrations – ShortStack Support
notes: Also 'Form Integrations' article (234443468). One event type (new entry). Corroborated via search snippets; direct fetch blocked by Cloudflare.

claim: Entry Restrictions: visitor IP address determines country; widget-level country visibility (default all countries; per-country picker); entry limits keyed on email address (one-time entry, frequency-based limits, maximum entry caps); reCAPTCHA settings in Form Container. Positioned as spam/lead-quality controls.
notes: Country-level IP geo only; no state-level targeting, no GPS/VPN detection documented. Enforcement is at the hosted-campaign/widget layer.

claim: Age gate is self-assembled from builder primitives: add a Date custom field, then an Action Widget displays the campaign to visitors meeting the age requirement or shows a message/redirects those who don't; 'Age Verification Gated Giveaway' template available. Self-attested DOB — no verification against identity data.
page_title: How to Add an Age Gate – ShortStack Support
notes: Corroborated by search snippets. Terms require 'legally-sufficient age-based restrictions' for age-sensitive content but the tooling is a DIY date-field gate.

claim: Fraud Filter mechanics: admin manually authors patterns (one per line, ? and * wildcards) matched against selected fields (email, physical address fields; IP address always searched); actions are label/flag or 'Reject Entry'; rejected entrants still see a 'Thanks for submitting' page while the entry never appears in the entry list.
page_title: Prohibit Fraudulent and Spam Entries with Fraud Filter Feature – ShortStack Support
notes: Audit-relevant: silently rejected attempts are not visible to the customer — denied 'decisions' leave no customer-accessible record.

claim: Instant Win: enabled per form; Simple mode (same prize/code, total count) or Advanced (Scale plan+) assigning unique prizes via uploaded code lists; explicit statement 'You cannot change the odds of winning' (prize count vs unknown entry volume); Advanced Settings allow prize-distribution weighting and day-restricted distribution.
notes: No seeded-winner certification or regulator-facing odds documentation; distribution controls are marketing-grade, not compliance-grade.

claim: Live Nation Entertainment (enterprise customer) uses ShortStack for sweepstakes, contests, RSVP forms, instant win, consent forms, and hosting contest rules; marketing director uses it 'dozens of times a day'; they run a 'review approve publish process' for legal-compliance oversight before campaigns go live ('I have more oversight').
page_title: Live Nation Entertainment Leverages ShortStack's Hassle-Free Customization and Compliance Features for Contest Success
notes: The 'compliance features' are permission-gated publishing + rules hosting used by the customer's own team — not vendor legal review or a formal counsel sign-off record.

claim: ShortStack for Teams: four main roles plus customizable per-member permissions, including 'Approve Entries' (approve/reject) and 'Publish' (publish campaigns/emails); account Owner owns all assets and controls subscription/transfers; permission tags grant access to tagged resources; client tagging for agencies; invites expire after 72 hours.
notes: RBAC exists and can gate publishing (basis of the Live Nation review workflow); no evidence of an approval-record/audit-trail feature attached to it.

claim: Winner selection: 'Pick Random Entries/Winner(s)' action with configurable number of winners, tracking labels (default 'picked [date]'), optional extra chances weighted by votes/points, and pre-draw filtering/moderation of entries; marketed as giving every eligible entrant an equal chance.
page_title: How to Select Winners - ShortStack Help Center
notes: Self-serve random picker; no third-party certified/witnessed drawing service, no drawing certificate artifact documented (unlike RandomPicker.com-style certification).

claim: Terms & Conditions: users' use 'shall comply with all applicable federal, state and local laws' and users are 'solely responsible' for compliance/familiarity with such laws; liability capped at 3x most recent monthly fee; prohibited content includes gambling-related content and age-sensitive material without 'legally-sufficient age-based restrictions'; users indemnify Pancake (ShortStack's legal entity) for claims arising from their content.
notes: Legal responsibility for promotion compliance is contractually pushed entirely onto the customer; ShortStack takes no administrator-of-record role.

claim: Entry Details view per entry: name/email; location and IP address; entry information including source and submission time; referral link URL; click-to-filter on any attribute (e.g., all entries from 'US'); admin can add labels or delete the entry.
notes: Entry records tie submitted facts + IP + timestamp together, but records are admin-deletable (not immutable) and no rule/policy version is attached.

claim: FAQ: all collected data exportable as CSV anytime ('You own your data'); ShortStack 'gives you the tools to stay compliant with Meta's promotion guidelines, but users should familiarize themselves with platform guidelines independently'; entry restrictions via email (one-time, frequency, caps). No AMOE, prize fulfillment, winner tax, or SLA content.
notes: Compliance posture = tooling + user responsibility, scoped to social-platform promotion guidelines rather than law.

claim: GDPR tooling: opt-in checkbox fields in the form designer; double opt-in confirmation links in autoresponders/scheduled emails; account-level 'Require Double Opt-In' applying to all lists; opt-in status indicators in lists and exports.
page_title: ShortStack and the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) – ShortStack Support
notes: Data-privacy consent capture is the deepest 'compliance' machinery in the product; promotion-law equivalents (eligibility, registration, AMOE) have no comparable tooling.

claim: Unique code distribution and redemption: upload code lists (help notes code lists on 'Pro Plan and higher' — legacy naming; pricing now gates code redemption at Scale); single-use unique codes distributed via emails or Instant Win; redemptions trackable back to the specific customer and campaign; 'Setting Up Code Redemption' documents a redemption flow.
page_title: Setting Up Code Redemption – ShortStack Support
notes: Closest thing to entitlement provenance: code -> campaign -> customer traceability. No wallet, balances, or value ledger.

claim: Analytics: visits/sessions/conversions funnel, total vs unique entries, traffic sources with UTM tracking, share tracking by platform, device breakdown (desktop/mobile/tablet), engagement (votes, clicks, video views, custom actions), real-time data; GA4 and Facebook Pixel connections.
notes: Marketing analytics, not audit logging; device data is segmentation, not device-intelligence risk signal.

claim: Points for Actions: campaign-scoped points for follows, video views, website visits, referrals, shares (enabled in form Advanced tab; recorded only after form submission); Refer-a-Friend issues unique share links and awards configurable bonus points that become extra vote totals or bonus entries.
notes: Per-campaign tally used for contest chances — not a persistent wallet/ledger, no balance semantics, no cross-campaign state.

claim: Absence finding (labeled inference): targeted searches of the help center and site on 2026-08-18 found no AMOE/mail-in entry workflow, no winner affidavit/W-9/1099 or tax-reporting features, no physical prize-fulfillment service, no certified-drawing service, no SSO/SAML, no policy/rules versioning, no decision or campaign-management API, no simulation/replay tooling, and no regulatory-change monitoring product. The documented integration surface (read-only Entries API + new-entry webhooks + embed + CSV) and the docs' enumeration of the anti-fraud suite support treating these as genuinely absent rather than merely unmentioned.
page_title: ShortStack Help Center | Campaign & Contest Support
notes: Methodology: multiple targeted WebSearch queries (AMOE, affidavit/W-9/1099, SSO/SAML, API create/POST, certified drawing) each returned competitor or generic results, none from ShortStack. Used to justify reasoned 0 scores; each such score is flagged as inference in the report.

claim: Instant Win marketing page: spin-to-win wheels, scratch-off cards, slot-machine reels; unique prizes per winner, static prize pools, coupon-code distribution; automatic winner notifications, prize claim management, campaign analytics; page contains no mention of odds disclosure, age/geo compliance, or fraud controls.
notes: Marketing page silent on compliance even for the most regulated mechanic (instant win), consistent with compliance being customer responsibility.

claim: Publishing: one-click publish/republish of campaigns; campaigns can be tested or shown to clients/team before publishing (builder preview, shareable standalone URLs); no separate staging/production environment system documented.
notes: Preview/test-before-publish is the closest analog to simulation/dry-run; there is no policy-level simulation because there is no policy layer.
